scenes.heading: Writing a pitch that actually gets read

sents.d: Writing a pitch that actually gets read
A specific idea for their product beats a generic 'I'd love to work with you.'
A pitch email that only says you're available and shares a portfolio link blends into a brand's inbox.
Including one specific, concrete content idea for their actual product signals you've done real homework and makes it easy for them to say yes.
Keep the pitch short — a brand marketer skimming dozens of these has no patience for a long biography.
State who you are, the specific idea, a portfolio link, and starting rate in a few sentences.
Following up once after about a week, if there's no response, is normal and expected — most replies to cold pitches come on the follow-up, not the first message.

take: Send short, specific pitches and follow up after a week.
